notes.title: Grounding the Power System
notes.notes:
In Darklight Breach, we want both the player’s and enemy’s ships to feel integral to gameplay—not just as static settings where combat takes place. To that end, ship construction has been a major focus, and recently, we’ve revisited our assumptions about how ship power should work.

Our first pass at a ship power system was modeled after FTL, specifically the concept of a global power pool that stations draw from to function. While this initially seemed like a solid approach, it created issues for enemy ships. If your squad infiltrates a room to disable an enemy weapon station, where do you target the power source? Do you have to take out every generator on the ship?

To address these issues, we’ve updated our power system to be local rather than global. Stations are now either powered or unpowered, and to ensure every active station has a generator nearby, power no longer passes through walls.

We believe this change will give players a new objective when boarding enemy ships while also adding an extra layer of strategy to ship-building decisions.

notes.title: First Steps to Deeper Strategy: The Alien Scout
notes.notes:
Hello! 

Welcome to the first of what will become regular updates on Darklight Breach. Our goal with these posts is to keep you informed about development progress and, most importantly, hear your feedback. So, don’t hesitate to share your thoughts—your input helps shape the game!

Let’s dive into our first update.

One thing we've consistently heard is the need for more strategic depth in crew combat and we couldn’t agree more. To tackle this, we decided to start by expanding the AI variety—because let’s face it, one enemy type just isn’t going to cut it.

Enter: the Alien Scout and ship alarm system.

The Scout patrols the ship, searching for intruders. If it spots your crew, it will become alerted (❗) and make a dash for the nearest alarm station. If the alarm is triggered, nearby alien goons jacked on adrenaline (⚡) will rush to hunt you down. These adrenalized aliens are tougher to deal with, so you’ll need to think tactically to avoid—or neutralize—the Scout before things escalate.

[previewyoutube=P-5Dos8E8Rg;full][/previewyoutube]

That's it for this post. Let us know what you think!
